    Davey Lopes, the legendary Los Angeles Dodgers second baseman and four-time All-Star, died on April 8, 2026, at the age of 80. According to reports, he passed away in Rhode Island following a long battle with complications from Parkinson's disease. 
    • Cause of Death: Complications from Parkinson’s disease.
    • Location: He was in his home state of Rhode Island, surrounded by family.
    • Career Highlights: A key member of the Dodgers' famed 1970s/80s infield, he was a 1981 World Series champion and a premier base stealer with 557 career stolen bases.
    • Post-Playing Career: Lopes was a dedicated coach and manager, known for mentoring young players. 
    He is remembered as a cornerstone of Dodgers history and a respected figure across MLB.

    What did Davey Lopes pass away from?
    Parkinson's disease
    Lopes was of Cape Verdean and Irish descent. He has a recreation center named after him in Providence, Rhode Island. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer following a routine physical in February 2008. Lopes died in Rhode Island on April 8, 2026, at the age of 80, due to complications from Parkinson's disease.
